rationale: The first turn was excellent: it correctly ranked a snapped belt as most likely and asked exactly the right unplugged hand-turn check, and the second turn correctly concluded 'the drum drive belt having snapped or come off' and sensibly flagged the jockey pulley. However, it then fired a fire-risk 'Stop using this appliance' card and insisted on 'a qualified appliance engineer' purely because of a 'slight rubber smell at the time', a smell it itself attributed to the belt letting go; the ground truth has no critical safety stop and treats belt/jockey pulley replacement as reasonable DIY. It never asked for the full model number for ordering nor whether the customer was comfortable removing panels, so a homeowner ends up paying an engineer for a cheap DIY belt. No fabrication, unsafe advice or looping, but the escalation was unwarranted and ended progress.
